sources.citation: Sutton, Peter. 1978. Wik: Aboriginal society, territory and language at Cape Keerweer, Cape York Peninsula, Australia. PhD thesis, University of Queensland.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Nganhcara/Uwanh/Muminh: cites 'Johnson (1974) on Kugu-Uwanh and Wik-Iiyanh, Martin (1968..) on Kugu-Uwanh, Kugu-Muminh..', Oates & Healey (1960), Sayers (?1969), von Sturmer lexical data; states Kugu-Uwanh and Kugu-Muminh are dialects of one language. Its stress appendix (pp. 235-236) is on Wik-Ngathan, not Kugu Nganhcara.

sources.citation: Smith, Ian & Steve Johnson. 1986. Sociolinguistic patterns in an unstratified society: the patrilects of Kugu Nganhcara. Linguistica Atlantica (Journal of the Atlantic Provinces Linguistic Association) 8: 29-43.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Open access (journals.lib.unb.ca, article/download/32408/1882527618), 15 pp., text layer extracted to. Section 3.1 'Phonology' (pp. 35-36) gives Table 3 inventory (5 vowels short and long, voiced/voiceless stop contrast, labio-velars) and inter-patrilect differences; the only prosody-adjacent remark is that long vs short vowel contrast is 'generally restricted to initial syllables' (p. 36). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the article.

sources.note: Phonology section is consonant and vowel tables only; no stress statement; references are Smith & Johnson 2000 (HAL 5: 357-507) and Smith & Johnson 1986.
